before.text: The scientist he bought a company to hire went on to mentor Edwin Land, who built Polaroid into the company Eastman might have built with a second chance: instant chemistry inside a consumer camera, defended by patents, run by a founder who was himself the product. Land sued Kodak for copying him and won the largest patent judgment American courts had produced, landing at the exact moment Kodak needed capital to go digital. It was the first serious wound. Land was then pushed out of his own company and lived to watch digital take it; Polaroid went bankrupt in 2001, eleven years before Kodak did. Land's most devoted student was Steve Jobs, who called him a hero, borrowed his model, and was cast out of his own company the same way. In 2012, when Kodak's patents were auctioned in bankruptcy for a fraction of the asking price, Apple was among the buyers.

before.name: the outline
before.label: before the essay
before.text: The scientist he bought a company to hire went on to mentor Edwin Land, who built Polaroid into the company Eastman might have built with a second chance: instant chemistry inside a consumer camera, defended by patents, run by a founder who was himself the product. Land sued Kodak for copying him and won the largest patent judgment American courts had produced, landing at the exact moment Kodak needed capital to go digital. It was the first serious wound. Land was then pushed out of his own company and lived to watch digital take it; Polaroid went bankrupt in 2001, eleven years before Kodak did. Land's most devoted student was Steve Jobs, who called him a hero, borrowed his model, and was cast out of his own company the same way. In 2012, when Kodak's patents were auctioned in bankruptcy for a fraction of the asking price, Apple was among the buyers.
before.passage: The scientist Eastman bought a company to hire went on to mentor Edwin Land, who built Polaroid into the company Eastman might have built with a second chance: instant chemistry inside a consumer camera, defended by patents, run by a founder who was himself the product. Land sued Kodak for copying him and won 925 million dollars, the largest patent judgment American courts had ever produced and the largest for the next quarter century. Land was then forced out of Polaroid after the Polavision failure and resigned the chairmanship in 1982. Polaroid filed for bankruptcy in October 2001, eleven years ahead of Kodak, killed by digital and by the debt it had taken on to fight off a hostile takeover.
